title: Cuju
summary: Cuju, 'kick the ball', is a football pastime from ancient China, played for more than two thousand years. Players kept a stuffed leather ball in the air with feet and body, and in some forms they aimed it at an opening in a goal hung between two tall posts.
howToPlay: Press and hold, then pull back: a ring shows where the ball will land.
Let go when the ring sits over the round hole in the red silk.
Eight kicks make a round and a match is two rounds.
rules: A round is eight kicks; a match is two rounds and the scores add up.
A ball that flies through the gold-rimmed hole scores 4.
A ball that strikes the silk but misses the hole scores 1.
A ball that goes wide of the screen scores nothing, and each kick stands alone.
Hand sway and a slight drop move the ball away from the ring, so a steady hold helps.
Stars are earned for 14, 28 and 40 points over a match.
heritageNote: Cuju began as a military training exercise and became a pastime of the Han, Tang and Song courts and streets, enjoyed by people of every rank. It is kept alive in China today as a cultural heritage sport and in demonstration matches.
